feedback: Written before this robot has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The evidence: iteration 5 (wheel_track 0.10, ±0.06 m row, 12 mm, kp 5, ki 0.1, kd 0.8, weights ±1.5/±0.75) gave 20 of 20 oval finishes and s-bend progress 0.42, with the slalom losing the line once per run. Iteration 8 (0.10 m, ±0.07 m row) fell to 9 of 20 on the oval and 0.18 on the s-bend, so the wider row costs the oval. Iteration 7 (0.09 m, ±0.07 m) fell to 3 of 20. Iteration 4 showed that ki 0.3 cut the oval finish rate, so controller authority is also a limit. Iteration 6 showed a 0.016 footprint is not the lever. The controller is held at iteration 5's values, so the track change is the only variable. Decision rules for iteration 11: if the oval finish rate is at least 0.85 and the s-bend progress is at or above 0.42, keep 0.09 m and try wheel_track 0.085 m or 0.08 m next. If the oval falls below 0.85, return to 0.10 m, which is the known-good geometry.
requested_changes: If the oval finish rate is at least 0.85 and s-bend progress rises above 0.42 with max_error near 0.061 m, keep the ±0.06 m row and narrow wheel_track to 0.085 m, since the track is the turn-rate lever (iteration 5 moved s-bend progress from 0.17 to 0.42 for a 0.02 m reduction).

If the oval finish rate falls below 0.85 at 0.09 m with the ±0.06 m row, return wheel_track to 0.10 m, the known-good iteration 5 geometry. Iteration 7's collapse was confounded by the ±0.07 m row, so the oval result here is the first clean test of the narrower track.

If the slalom still loses the line about once per run at 0.09 m, do not widen the row past ±0.06 m, because iteration 8 showed ±0.07 m costs the oval. Test sensor y spacing (for example, moving the row from y=0.08 to a tighter centre cluster at the same ±0.06 m span) instead.
